newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: UOP revamping half of China's refineries.
newsitem.headline: UOP revamping half of China's refineries.

text.p: UOP, a partnership between Allied Signal Inc and Union Carbide Corp, is helping modernise almost half of China's 65 refineries, a senior company official said on Friday.
The company is also working with other Asian refiners to optimise output at a time when profits are under considerable pressure, Richard Wilmoth, UOP's managing director in Asia, told reporters.

"We are working closely with Sinopec in terms of...modernisation of their refineries and there is a huge potential for our business in terms of developing the right piece of technology we can supply," he said.
Speaking at the opening of its Singapore office, Wilmoth said UOP had "involvements with about 30 refineries" in China.
China, Asia's second largest refiner, has a production capacity of 4.3 million barrels-per-day (bpd) but produces between 3.0 and 3.2 million bpd, analysts said.
"In terms of efficiency with which they run...it doesn't meet world class standards," UOP president and CEO Michael Winfield said.
"It does say there are many opportunities get a lot of growth out of the exisiting facilities if they are modernised, operated and maintained to world class standard."
UOP is the world's leading supplier and licenser of technologies to oil and gas related industries.
Over the past year or tow, Asian refiners have been grappling with refining losses due to regional over capacity.
UOP is currently working to introduce new catalyst and "improve control schemes and detailed review of the process technology to improve margins", Wilmoth said.
Such improvements would add between US 50 cents and $1 to profits on each barrel, he said revenue.
"Right now we have a major focused effort in Japan because of the very severe pressure Japanese refiners find themselves under," Wilmoth said.
UOP saw 1996 revenues grow by about 10 percent to U.S.$1.1 billion, with almost half coming from the Asia-Pacific region.

Its technology was used in the 100,000-bpd Malacca refinery in Malaysia which is due to start production in 1998 and for the planned 125,000-bpd Sukhothai refinery in Thailand due to come on stream in 2000.
